9400 Series Drop Weight Impact Tester 
last updated：Oct 31, 2022 
 インストロンジャパンカンパニイリミテッド 日本支社 
 Official site 
Instrumentation drop weight impact testing machine. It supports a wide range of tests from materials to components, including Charpy, Izod, punching, and CAI tests (compression after impact). 
The 9400 series has been developed to provide faster results, fewer errors, and lower training costs for customers at the forefront of high-quality advanced materials development, particularly in laboratories focused on the development of high-strength and lightweight products.
The 9400 series drop weight impact testers comply with all major impact testing standards ranging from 0.3J to 1800J.
They feature a simple operating procedure, preset test conditions and guided testing, streamlined data management, output for analytical data, and compatibility with high-speed cameras.
With these features, Instron's 9400 series drop weight impact testers become simpler, smarter, and safer.
*For more details, please download the PDF or contact us.

basic information 
The puncture test, CAI test (compression after impact), tensile impact test, three-point bending test, and wedge delamination impact test are the most common drop weight impact testing methods. These tests determine the toughness of polymers, the load-deflection curve, and the total energy absorption during impact events. The main ISO and ASTM standards related to plastic impact testing include ASTM D3763 for multiaxial impact testing, ISO 6603 for puncture test methods, ASTM D7136 for CAI test methods, ISO 11343 for wedge delamination impact test methods, and ISO 8256 for tensile impact test methods.

Applications/Examples of results 
Impact analysis of hand tools, impact of soccer shoe outsoles, impact characteristics of polycrystalline diamond cutters, impact resistance of saw teeth, measurement of adhesive bond strength under impact according to ISO 11343 (wedge-peel test), impact resistance of hip protectors, impact testing of equestrian equipment for horseback riding sports, impact behavior of rigid plastics under puncture according to ISO 6603-2, impact resistance of plastic shotgun shell fillers, impact of golf club grips, impact testing of fiber-reinforced cement, safety for counterattacking according to BS EN 13277, drop weight impact testing of rocks and ores, high-capacity tensile impact testing, impact testing of molded plastic tanks according to AS/NZS 4766, impact characteristics of pharmaceutical tablets, impact characteristics of concrete beams, impact characteristics of roof tiles, edgewise drop impact of LCD glass panels, compressive impact resistance of composites for maritime applications, high-speed impact testing of dashboards, Airbus test method for determining compressive strength after impact according to AITM, impact characteristics of mouthpieces, impact testing of orthopedic implants, etc.

(Free) Instron WEB Seminar Series: Do you know the term component testing? ~ With Instron, you can test even large finished parts. 
Seminar・Event 
**Presenter:** Shimpei Yamashita, Instron Japan, Materials Testing Division
**Seminar Summary:** 
When we think of a "three-point bending test," we usually imagine a test where a static compressive load is applied. By placing a specimen on a bending fixture and dropping a tap (impact rod) from a certain height to apply an impact, we can conduct a dynamic bending impact test. Furthermore, these tests can be performed not only on thin sheets and dumbbell specimens but also on components (finished parts), allowing for tests that are more suited to actual usage environments. This seminar will introduce the "three-point bending" and "component" impact tests.
**Target Audience for the Seminar:** 
- Those considering testing not only thin sheets and dumbbell specimens but also large finished parts. 
- Individuals who are hearing the term "three-point bending impact test" for the first time. 
- Those who want to safely conduct impact tests on large specimens and observe the impact behavior. 
- Customers considering the Instron 9400 series and Bluehill Impact software.

(Free) Instron Web Seminar Series: Impact Testing Followed by Compression Testing, Compression Testing During Impact Testing - What Can Be Learned by Applying Impact and Compression to Test Specimens 
Seminar・Event 
**Presenter:** Shimpei Yamashita, Instron Japan, Materials Testing Division
**Seminar Summary:** 
Are you familiar with the "CAI" test? It is a common testing method for composite materials primarily used in aircraft wings, as defined by testing standards such as ASTM. In Japanese, it is referred to as the post-impact compression test, which involves conducting both a drop weight impact test and a static compression test. I will explain why such tests are necessary and how they are actually carried out. Additionally, I will provide specific examples related to compression impact testing.
**Target Audience for the Seminar:**
- Those who have heard of the CAI test but want to know how it is specifically conducted.
- Those interested in how to capture the dynamics of the impact test using high-speed cameras.
- Those who want to learn about specific examples and fixtures related to compression impact testing.
- Customers considering the Instron 9400 series and Bluehill Impact software.

(Free) Instron WEB Seminar Series: Not Just Punching Tests. New Applications of the Drop Weight Impact Testing Machine - Wedge Delamination Test & Tensile Impact Test 
Seminar・Event 
**Presenter:** Shimpei Yamashita, Instron Japan, Materials Testing Division
When it comes to peel tests and tensile tests, many people may think of "static tests." While conducting tests at low speeds is common, in actual usage environments, instantaneous impacts occur, making evaluations through "dynamic tests" such as peeling or tensile tests important. This seminar will focus on peel impact tests and tensile impact tests conducted with a drop weight impact testing machine, and will introduce real-world examples of industries where these tests are performed.
**Target Audience for the Seminar:**
- Those who want to understand why dynamic peel impact tests and tensile impact tests are necessary.
- Those who want to know what standards exist and under what testing conditions they are conducted.
- Customers considering the Instron 9400 series and Bluehill Impact software.

Instron was founded in 1946 by Harold Hindman and George Bahl, who were conducting joint research at MIT (Massachusetts Institute of Technology) at the time. They developed the world's first electromechanical (screw-type) universal testing machine. The name "Instron" is derived from "instrument" and "electronics."
Instron's product range offers diversity that can cater to almost all global markets and industries, and since its establishment, over 70 years of testing technology and manufacturing experience have been built, with more than 50,000 systems operating worldwide.
In 1965, Instron Japan was established to support customers in Japan. Currently, it has major bases in the United States, Europe, and Asia, providing sales and services in 40 languages through agents in 160 countries around the world.
